phase1.explanation:
[[term:Packages]] are how Java organizes classes into namespaces, the same way folders organize files on your computer.

A `package` declaration [[key:must be the very first line in a file]] (before even imports), and the convention is a reversed domain name — `com.mycompany.util` — specifically so two different companies' code can never accidentally collide under the same package name.

Once a class lives in a package, anything that wants to use it needs an `import` — `import com.mycompany.util.MathUtils;` pulls in exactly that one class, while `import com.mycompany.util.*;` pulls in everything in that package. [[key:There's exactly one package Java imports for you automatically]]: `java.lang`, which is why `String`, `System`, and `Math` all just work without any import at all.

Everything else — `java.util` for Scanner/ArrayList/HashMap, `java.io` for file handling, `java.time` for dates — needs an explicit import, or you can skip the import entirely and use a [[term:fully qualified name]] instead, writing out the whole path every time, like `java.util.ArrayList<String>()`.

[[key:Why bother organizing code this way at all]]? Mainly to avoid naming collisions — two unrelated libraries can both have a class called `Vector` and never conflict, as long as they live in different packages — plus it keeps related classes grouped logically instead of scattered.

phase2.explanation:
[[warn:ArrayList lives in java.util, and java.util is NOT automatically imported]] — only `java.lang` gets that free pass. Without an explicit import, the compiler has genuinely never heard of `ArrayList`.

[[key:The fix is one line at the top of the file]]: `import java.util.ArrayList;`. Or, if you'd rather skip the import, you can always use the fully qualified name directly: `java.util.ArrayList<String> list = new java.util.ArrayList<>();` — more to type, but it works without any import at all.

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a package structure:
• com.example.shapes
• In it, create Rectangle and Circle classes with area() methods
• In a Main class (can be in same file), import and use both shapes

Note: For simplicity, we'll put everything in one file with package declarations.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: the reverse-domain-name convention for packages (com.mycompany.util) isn't just a popular habit — it's an official recommendation baked right into Oracle's Java Language Specification, specifically so that as long as everyone owns their own domain name, two companies' package names can never accidentally collide.
